Commentary.Commentary: That's it from our side. Hope you enjoyed our coverage! Do join us for the 3rd ODI at Dambulla on 28th August at 1430 local time. Till then, goodbye and take care!

Australian captain, Steven Smith thinks they didn't execute it well with the ball. Credits Sri Lanka for batting so well as they scored almost 300 on such wicket. Adds Aponso is a very talented bowler. Says they just have to build more partnerships. Informs there is always pressure but wants his guys to adapt better. Credits Faulkner for picking wickets towards the end but at the same time says the damage was already done.

Man of the Match, Angelo Mathews credits Chandimal and Mendis as they set the platform. Says he just asked Kusal Perera to enjoy out there. Adds the wicket was good to bat on, although it spun a bit. Credits Aponso for the way he bowled. He is happy with his youngsters like de Silva and Mendis.

Wade and Head fought it out in the middle and scored a crucial 50-run partnership. When the stand was starting to look threatening, Wade departed to a low full toss from Perera and it pushed Australia further on the back foot. Sri Lanka put the shackles on the visitors after that and the lower order tumbled under pressure. The home side has proved their worth and are the deserved winners.

It was Thisara Perera who took the crucial wickets of Warner and Finch and put the Australians on the back foot from the beginning. He paved the way for his fellow bowlers to apply pressure on the middle order and they did it with quite a lot of authority. Aponso was terrific with his variations and the Aussies found it really difficult to read him. Smith and Bailey fell to his magical spell and it was always going to be an uphill task for the Aussies from there on.

Sri Lanka have bounced back hard and they have done it in great style to LEVEL THE SERIES 1-1! They outplayed the Aussies comprehensively and have stormed to the biggest victory against them in terms of runs (82 runs). It was a well rounded performance by their seamers as well as spinners as they bamboozled the Men in Yellow with their brilliant bowling efforts.
